This is first application for grant of anticipatory bail under section 438 of Cr.P.C. on behalf of the applicant who is apprehending his arrest in connection with FIR/Crime No.644/2023 dated 20.10.2023 registered at Police Station Koh-E-Fiza, District Bhopal, for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC & Section 4 of Muslim Women Protection of Rights on Marriage Act.

sentences.text: Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant may be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.
3. On the contrary, learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case-diary.
5.

On perusal of the case diary, it is revealed that offence under Section 498-A of IPC and Section 4 of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 is registered against the applicant, who is the husband of complainant.

entities.text: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The marriage was solemnized between the applicant and complainant in the year 2009 and the marital disputes arose between them.
According to the complainant, she was being treated with cruelty by her husband, but there is no medical report to suggest the physical cruelty despite the allegations about it.

It is claimed in the FIR that applicant gave Talaq to his wife by pronouncing Talaq thrice instantaneously and for declaration of this divorce, he filed a civil suit but facts reveal that this case was withdrawn prior to filing of FIR.
6.

It is claimed by the complainant that on 24.04.2023, applicant again told the complainant that he has given her Takaq, but taking into consideration that prior to this episode, applicant had filed a civil suit for seeking declaration of divorce, this allegation has been seriously challenged by the applicant husband.
7.

Further, there was a divorce petition filed by the complainant herself, although she has claimed that she filed that petition upon being threatened by applicant but looking to her age and maturity,
applicant has challenged this fact also.

The applicant has relied upon the compromise petition entered into between the two parties on 21.04.2023 and a relinquish deed regarding the property executed by the applicant in favour of complainant dated 25.04.2023.
According to him, after execution of this deed, the complainant wife has withdrawn her divorce petition.
8. Taking into consideration these facts in their entirety, this Court is of the opinion that the applicant has made out a case for anticipatory bail, therefore, this application is allowed.

9. It is directed that in the event of arrest of applicant by the police in the aforesaid crime, he shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer) for his regular appearance before the Police/Arresting Officer during the investigation or before the Court during trial.

10. It is directed that the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 438(2)
of Cr.P.C., failing which this order shall automatically stand cancelled without further reference to the Court.
11. Accordingly, the M.Cr.C stands allowed and disposed of.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE sjk Mohd. Rehan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/118364280/
